answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because harbor only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, ferrous is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any yarrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
